skill.name: onvifscan
skill.description: Guide authorized ONVIF security assessments by checking endpoint authentication and testing credentials with the external onvifscan command.
skill.summary: Assess ONVIF authentication and weak credentials on devices you own or have permission to test.
skill.author: BrownFineSecurity

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks or private-network examples. Six examples direct external scanner execution, while credential brute-forcing and potentially destructive tests lack mandatory authorization controls.

remediation.issue: The workflow can perform credential attacks without requiring proof of authorization.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit authorization, target scope, and lockout approval before generating or executing any brute-force command.

remediation.issue: The all-endpoints option may invoke potentially destructive device operations.
remediation.suggestion: Require separate confirmation for this option and present the affected endpoints before execution.

remediation.issue: User-supplied targets and file paths are placed into external command templates.
remediation.suggestion: Validate targets and paths, reject shell metacharacters, and invoke the scanner with argument arrays instead of shell interpolation.

content.value_statement: ONVIF cameras can expose services or use weak credentials. This skill guides authorized authentication checks and controlled credential tests with onvifscan.
actual_capabilities: Selects authentication checks or credential testing based on the assessment goal.
Collects the target address, scan type, and optional wordlist requirements.
Builds onvifscan commands for authentication checks and credential tests.
Supports verbose responses, alternative ports, and text, JSON, or quiet output.
Uses built-in or custom username and password wordlists for controlled tests.
Explains the all-endpoints option and its potentially destructive behavior.
limitations: Requires the external onvifscan tool from iothackbot and does not include its executable.
Does not automatically verify target ownership, authorization, or approved scope.
Credential testing may trigger account lockouts, monitoring alerts, or device rate controls.
The all-endpoints option may invoke destructive operations on some devices.

use_cases.title: Audit Camera Authentication
use_cases.description: Check whether managed cameras expose ONVIF endpoints without required authentication.

use_cases.title: Validate Credential Controls
use_cases.description: Run approved, rate-limited credential tests with client-provided wordlists and scope.

use_cases.title: Test Device Hardening
use_cases.description: Compare authentication behavior across firmware builds in an isolated test environment.

prompt_templates.title: Check Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: I am authorized to test [target]. Prepare a basic ONVIF authentication check and explain the expected result categories.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for unauthenticated endpoint access

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Detailed Responses
prompt_templates.prompt: I am authorized to test [target:port]. Plan a verbose authentication scan and summarize which response details may indicate exposed services.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of ONVIF XML responses

prompt_templates.title: Test Approved Credentials
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a rate-limited credential test for [target] using [username file] and [password file]. Confirm authorization and lockout limits before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Scoped Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an ONVIF assessment for [targets]. Separate safe checks from potentially destructive tests, define stop conditions, and require confirmation before execution.

output_examples.input: Check whether my lab camera requires ONVIF authentication.
output_examples.output: The assessment starts with the standard authentication check. Report each endpoint as protected, exposed, unreachable, or inconclusive.

output_examples.input: Test approved credentials without risking an account lockout.
output_examples.output: The plan confirms authorization, attempt limits, delay settings, stop conditions, and the approved wordlists before any credential test.

output_examples.input: Review a camera on a nonstandard port with detailed responses.
output_examples.output: The scan uses the supplied port and verbose mode. The summary highlights authentication status and relevant ONVIF response details.

best_practices: Obtain written authorization and define target scope before every scan.
Start with authentication checks and use credential testing only when explicitly approved.
Set attempt limits, stop conditions, and recovery plans before testing production devices.
anti_patterns: Do not scan internet hosts or third-party devices without explicit permission.
Do not enable all-endpoints testing on production devices without separate confirmation.
Do not use large wordlists when lockout behavior and device capacity are unknown.

faq.question: What devices can this skill assess?
faq.answer: It targets IP cameras and other devices that expose ONVIF services.

faq.question: Does the skill include onvifscan?
faq.answer: No. The external onvifscan command must already be available from the iothackbot installation.

faq.question: Is the authentication check non-destructive?
faq.answer: The standard check is described as non-destructive. The all-endpoints option may test destructive operations.

faq.question: Can it test weak credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports rate-limited credential testing with built-in or custom wordlists.

faq.question: Does it verify authorization?
faq.answer: No. Users must confirm ownership, permission, target scope, and lockout limits before testing.

faq.question: Which output formats are supported?
faq.answer: The documented formats are text, JSON, and quiet output.
